asDecan.p: Each sign is cut into three slices of ten degrees, called decans, and each slice gets a planet and a small card of its own. Your Sun sits in the first ten degrees of Cancer, and in the Golden Dawn order that stretch goes to Venus. Venus has no special standing in Cancer. It isn't at home there and it isn't weakened either, it's more of a guest, and like any guest it picks up the manners of the house, which in Cancer means the Moon's moods. So you get Cancer at its freshest, cardinal water that wants to get things started, with a liking for pleasure and for people added in. The Three of Cups next along belongs to Mercury and is chattier. The Four belongs to the Moon itself and turns further inward. Yours is the slice that reaches out to one person. The Chariot is your Sun card, the wide view of Cancer, and this is the finer grain inside it. Look at the two people in the picture, cups raised, standing at the same height.

You notice who's been left out. At a family dinner you're the one who clocks that your brother-in-law hasn't said a word since the entrée, and somehow you've ended up next to him by dessert. You remember how people take their tea, and it bothers you a little when they don't remember yours. A text left on read gets to you more than you'd admit, and you'll reread your own message twice to work out what you did wrong. You like the house to feel good to walk into, the right lamp on, something in the oven, and you'll put more thought into a friend's birthday present than into your own tax return. Big groups are fine, but you're really waiting for the part of the night when it drops to two of you on the back step. The care is real, and it's also something you enjoy.

The gift people don't clock is that you're brave about closeness. Cancer gets called shy, and the later degrees can be, but with Venus in the cardinal opening of the sign you're usually the one who goes first. After two old friends fall out, you're the one who rings eight months later and says 'this is silly, come for lunch'. You'll tell someone you like them. You'll say sorry before you're sure it was your fault, because the gap bothers you more than being right does. That makes you the person who holds friendship groups and families together over decades, often without anyone saying so. I see this a lot with early Cancer Suns. Half the reunions in their circle happened because they sent the first message.

This one's harder to spot because it looks like kindness. Venus likes things pleasant, and in Cancer it also wants to feel safe, so you can get very good at keeping the peace by quietly doing more. You'll host Christmas again even though you said last year was the last time. You'll agree to the restaurant you didn't want. Then months later something small tips it, and all of it comes out at once, the Christmases and the restaurant included, and the other person has no idea where it came from. The other side of it is that you can shrink your world down to one or two people. When you're in a good couple or a close friendship, everyone else gets a bit less of you, and some friends feel it well before you do.

When something hurts, you go home, usually literally. You cancel the drinks, pull the curtains, make the soup your mum used to make, and let one person in at most. That first retreat does you good. A week later it's often gone a bit sideways. You're still in, still going over the conversation in your head, and you've started comforting other people so you don't have to look at your own thing. A friend's small crisis gets two hours of your evening while your big one waits. The people close to you can feel shut out, because you're warm and busy and not actually telling them anything. What helps is letting someone look after you back, and saying out loud what happened. A meal someone else cooks. A walk by water, if there's any near you, does more than it should.

You're romantic in the old sense. You like the rituals, the same table at the same place, the song, the anniversary nobody else would remember. Cancer's opposite sign is Capricorn, so it's common for you to fall for people who look a bit cool from outside, the capable, busy type who shows love by turning up and paying the bills on time. It can work beautifully, but you'll need to hear the words sometimes, and they may have to learn that. The less obvious thing is how much of your love goes into feeding people and making a home, and how hurt you get when that goes unremarked. You'd take 'that was a lovely dinner' over flowers any day. Tell your partner that. Most of them have no idea.

Work goes best for you when there's a person on the other end of it. Hospitality, nursing, teaching small classes, hairdressing, finding someone a house they'll actually want to live in, account management where you've had the same clients for nine years and know their kids' names. Venus gives you a good eye as well, so a lot of early Cancers end up in interiors or food, anywhere that making a room or a plate feel good is the job. You're often the one in the office who organises the farewell card and knows who's going through a divorce. That's useful, and it's also unpaid work that can quietly eat your week. Asking for money is the hard part. Practise naming your rate, or the raise you want, to someone who'll tell you if you sounded apologetic.

At twenty this decan often gives a great deal to the wrong people. The friend who only rings when there's a problem, the partner who's lovely on weekends and vague the rest of the time. You keep trying because you can see who they could be. By the mid-thirties most people with the Sun here have learned to notice who gives back, and the circle gets smaller and better. A lot of them have made a proper home by then, whether that's a family or a flat that finally feels like theirs. In the fifties it tends to widen out again. The kids leave or the work settles, and the care goes further afield, into a community garden, a choir, the grandkids, the neighbour's dog. Often yours becomes the kitchen everyone ends up in.

Once a week for a month, let someone do something for you without doing anything back straight away. Let a friend pay for coffee and just say thanks. Let your partner cook and stay out of the kitchen. If someone offers you a lift, take it. When you feel the urge to even things up on the spot, notice where it sits in your body, usually the chest or the hands, and leave it there for a day. Then, if you still want to, return the favour.
